help: usage: fleet-switchboard install [-h] [--opencode OPENCODE] [--no-service] [--with-cloud-reaper] [--no-herdr-link] [--shared-profile] [--profile DIR] [--gh-user NAME] [--dry-run] [--uninstall] Idempotent. Each step says done, already done, or skipped (why). Finds an OpenCode v2 binary (never assumes `opencode` is v2), writes the config keys that are missing, puts the kit's agents, skills and plugins into a private v2 profile (never the directory your ordinary OpenCode reads, unless --shared- profile), links the herdr plugin, installs a service that keeps the daemon alive, then starts the daemon and prints `status`. No secret is written anywhere. options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --opencode OPENCODE The OpenCode v2 binary (absolute path); default: the configured one, then the known places --no-service Do not install the service --with-cloud-reaper Also install and load the cloud worker reaper as a service (opt-in: it needs a cluster login; its non- secret CW_* settings are copied from this environment) --no-herdr-link Do not link herdr's plugin (it starts the daemon whenever herdr starts) --shared-profile Put v2's pieces in the directory your ordinary OpenCode reads too (~/.config/opencode), which can break a v1 OpenCode that reads them. Default: a private profile --profile DIR The private profile's directory (absolute); default: $XDG_DATA_HOME/fleet-switchboard/profile --gh-user NAME The gh account the agents' token comes from (default: gh's active one) --dry-run Print every step; write nothing --uninstall Reverse the profile pieces, the herdr link and the service; config, state and sessions stay
